BusinessName.BusinessNameLine1Txt: Jacobs & Cushman San Diego Food Bank

IRS990.ActivityOrMissionDesc: Provide food to people in need, advocate for the hungry and educate the public about hunger issues.
IRS990.MissionDesc: To provide nutritious food to people in need, advocate for the hungry, and educate the public about hunger-related issues.
IRS990.Desc: The member agency program (also known as the food to nonprofits program) relies on partnerships with hundreds of nonprofit agencies in the community that help the San Diego Food Bank provide food assistance and support to hundreds of thousands of individuals and families who face food insecurity in the San Diego region. In the fiscal year ended 6/30/24, the San Diego Food Bank worked with more than 450 nonprofit partners that included food pantries, soup kitchens, shelters, low-income daycare centers, after school programs, senior centers, and disability programs to distribute food and nonfood items to people in need.

ProgSrvcAccomActy2Grp.Desc: The emergency food assistance program (EFAP, also known as TEFAP) is a federal program that provides monthly emergency and supplemental food to individuals and families who meet income guidelines set by the federal government. In the fiscal year ended 6/30/24, the San Diego Food Bank served an average of 85,000 individuals per month through the EFAP program and distributed over 12 million pounds of food inventory.

ProgSrvcAccomActy3Grp.Desc: The commodity supplemental food program (CSFP) is a federally supported program that provides food and nutrition education to seniors over the age of 60. The program provides participants with a 40-pound box of food every month that is filled with a variety of nutritious food items. In the fiscal year ended 6/30/24, the San Diego Food Bank served approximately 15,000 seniors every month and distributed just over 6 million pounds of food.

ProgSrvcAccomActyOtherGrp.Desc: The San Diego Food Bank operates several additional programs that distribute nutritious food to people in need, including the food 4 kids back pack program, farm to family (which distributes fresh produce,) and CalFresh outreach.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Schedule I, Part I, Line 2 Procedures for monitoring use of grant funds.
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Food Bank provides grants of food and non-food items to people in needthrough various programs. Through the Emergency Food Assistance Program (EFAP), monthly emergency and supplemental food is provided to individuals and families that meet income guidelines set by the Federal Government. The Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP) provides food to seniors over the age of 60 each month. The Food Bank verifies eligibility and ensures compliance with the program using on-site staff and technology. During FYE 6/30/24, the Food Bank distributed grocery store gift cards through its Client Choice Pantry which serves individuals and families whose income fell below 130% of the federal poverty line. Gift cards were also distributed to participants in need at distributions run by the Food Bank's network of nonprofit partners. The Food Bank regularly monitors these distributions for compliance and to ensure that distributions are serving populations in need.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 11b Review of form 990 by governing body
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: Form 990 is prepared by an independent CPA firm and reviewed in detail by the organization's top management. The reviewed Form 990 is then provided to the board of directors prior to filing with the IRS.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 12c Conflict of interest policy
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Conflict of Interest Policy is reviewed and signed annually by all board members, officers, and key employees. The Executive Assistant and CFO review the signed policies and questionnaires for potential conflicts. If a potential conflict is identified, it is evaluated by the Executive Committee of the Board. Directors involved in a conflict of interest will be excluded from discussion and will recuse themselves of any vote related to the conflict.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 15a Process to establish compensation of top management official
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The HR team of the Food Bank reviews salary information for the organization (including the CEO's position) on an annual basis. Comparability data in the form of a salary survey is used and presented to the Executive Committee of the Board. The Executive Committee presents a recommendation to the Board and the CEO's compensation is voted on and documented in the Board minutes.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 15b Process to establish compensation of other employees
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The HR team reviews salary information for all staff members annually, using comparability data in the form of a salary survey to set market rates for each position. The compensation for all other officers and key employees is approved by the CEO. The process is documented in the personnel budget and in human resource files.
